newsitem.title: UK: British Steel asks unions for work reform.
newsitem.headline: British Steel asks unions for work reform.

text.p: British Steel's chairman and chief executive Brian Moffat has warned trade unions of the need to cut jobs and reform work practices in order to ward off a series of threats to the business.

In a letter to union leaders, Moffat cited the threats as "exposure to fluctuating exchange rates and continued world steel overcapacity, but also the increasing threat to our competitiveness that comes from our traditional European competitors...and from low-cost economies in Eastern Europe."

The group intends to review all divisions with a view to scaling down employment. The chairman's letter said the group would review employment conditions "to reflect the individual capabilities of employees and the operating culture required."

Union and company bosses will meet on Friday to discuss the implications. British Steel has 53,000 employees worldwide, with 43,000 based in the UK. Since privatisation, British Steel has cut staff back from 200,000.
